Hello all

let's say i have a simple path model defined like this:

'outcome ~ factorA + FactorB + FactorC'

and i run it separately - once for the male participants and once for the female participants

is there a way to compare the regressions between the models? my instinct says no

i think that i would have to somehow include a dummy variable for gender into the model (so that i have one model ) but i have no idea how to go about it


using  sem( group = "gender)  only puts the two model results on the same output. 

thank you all for helping!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: comparing  regressions from two path models
parts: is there a way to compare the regressions between the models?

Yes, you can constrain the regression slope(s) to equivalence across groups by using the same label(s) across groups.  See the tutorial:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

To test the null hypothesis that the equality constraint is appropriate, you can also fit a model without the equality constrain, then calculate the chi-squared difference test using the anova() method.

Terry

constraining the slopes to be the same value ( using c(V1,V1)*X2 or even using the group.partial function ) i'll get the same slope value for both groups. 

if i understand you correctly, it's not the values themselves that matter, it's the anova() test between the two models.
Yes, if the change in chi-squared is significant, then the null hypothesis of equal slopes is rejected.
also, in the link there is a function called  measurementInvariance() - can that also help me?

No, regression slopes are not one of the types of parameters that are constrained when testing measurement invariance.
